faqs: Eligible new customers get the full RetainAI workspace for 14 days after completing checkout. A card is required and kept on file by Stripe. The C$20 monthly subscription starts automatically after the trial unless you cancel. Cancel in Settings → Billing before the trial end shown in your account to avoid the subscription charge. You can import contacts, try follow-ups, and connect supported services during the trial; those services may have their own fees or approval requirements.
Does RetainAI send messages without my approval?
You control how messages are sent. AI drafts can be reviewed and edited, while automations show their triggers and actions before you activate them.
Can I use my existing WhatsApp Business account?

RetainAI connects through Meta’s WhatsApp Business platform. Your account must meet Meta’s connection and approval requirements. Approved templates are used when a conversation is outside WhatsApp’s customer-service window. Meta’s messaging charges are separate from your RetainAI subscription.
Can I cancel or download my data?

Yes. Cancel from Settings → Billing or the Stripe billing portal. Workspace export and account-deletion controls are also available in Settings. Account deletion is separate from cancelling your subscription and includes a recovery window.
Is RetainAI only for large teams?
No. It is designed for owner-led and growing service businesses that want a clear system without enterprise CRM complexity.
Will AI sound exactly like me?
RetainAI uses your business context and tone preferences to prepare a useful draft. You can review and adjust the final message before sending.

/about.heading: Know who you’re trusting with your customer relationships.

sections.heading: Built around the customers you already know
sections.copy: Your next sale is often already in your customer list. RetainAI helps you see who needs a reply, who is ready to rebook and what to do next, with the customer’s history close at hand.

/retention-crm-for-service-businesses.intro: A customer retention CRM keeps each customer’s history and next action together. For a salon, home-service business or coach, that means fewer follow-ups left to memory and a clearer plan for repeat business.

sections.heading: From memory to a shared next step
sections.copy: A conversation in WhatsApp, a note on your phone and a booking in your calendar each tell part of the story. RetainAI brings the context together: the last conversation, what the customer needs and when to follow up.

sections.heading: A useful daily rhythm
sections.copy: Review the customers who need attention. Check their history, then reply, add an appointment or set a follow-up. AI can help draft the message; you review the words and decide what to send.

/find-customers-who-stopped-rebooking.heading: How to find customers who stopped rebooking
/find-customers-who-stopped-rebooking.intro: Most regulars don’t announce that they’ve stopped coming. Their next visit just never gets booked. This guide shows a simple way to spot them from records you already keep, with or without software, and how to follow up without pressure.

sections.heading: 1. Gather every customer’s completed visits
sections.copy: Start from what actually happened, not what was booked: completed appointments from your booking tool, calendar or receipts. Cancelled and no-show bookings tell a different story, so keep them apart. For each customer you need their name, how to contact them, and the dates of their completed visits.

sections.heading: 2. Work out each customer’s usual rhythm
sections.copy: Customers come back on their own schedule: one client books every three weeks, another every two months. With three or more completed visits, take the typical gap between them; the middle value is steadier than an average, because one late visit won’t skew it. With only one or two visits, use the usual interval for that service as a starting point.

sections.heading: 3. Flag who is past their usual time
sections.copy: Add the customer’s usual gap to their last completed visit. Anyone whose expected date has passed, and who has nothing booked, belongs on your list. Allow a little slack before acting so you don’t message people who are simply a few days late.

sections.heading: 4. Treat long-quiet customers separately
sections.copy: Someone who visited once and has been quiet for months is a different case from a regular who is a week overdue. Put long-quiet customers in their own win-back group so they get a gentler, less frequent message.

sections.heading: 5. Reach out personally, then record what happened
sections.copy: Send a short, personal note that mentions their last visit and makes rebooking easy, for example with a link to your booking page. Message only customers who have agreed to hear from you, include a way to opt out, and honour it. Note each reply, booking or ‘not now’ so the list stays accurate next week.

sections.heading: How RetainAI does this for you
sections.copy: RetainAI works out rebooking dates from each customer’s completed visits, using the usual time between them, and lists customers whose usual interval has nearly passed. Customers with no completed visit who have been inactive for 90 days or more appear as win-back candidates. AI can draft the follow-up; you review the words and decide what to send. Start by importing a CSV or vCard of the contacts you already have.
